title: 단어 첫소리 ㄷ·ㅌ·ㄸ: 소리 구별과 읽기
summary: Practice distinguishing and reading the word-initial Korean consonants ㄷ (plain), ㅌ (aspirated), and ㄸ (tense). Helpful English sound references are provided so beginners can connect the sounds and read simple words accurately.
objective: Learners will identify and pronounce ㄷ (plain), ㅌ (aspirated), and ㄸ (tense) in word-initial position, link them to clear English cues (ㄷ ≈ between English d and t with a light puff, ㅌ ≈ t in “top”, ㄸ ≈ tense t with no puff, close to the t in “stop”), and correctly read simple words containing these initials.
exercises: Choose the word that starts with ㄸ (tense): 두부 / 토끼 / 또
Look at the romanization and write only the first consonant in Hangul: dubu
Choose the word that means ‘daughter’: 달 / 딸
Choose the word that starts with ㅌ (aspirated): 달 / 토마토 / 딸
Look at the romanization and write only the first consonant in Hangul: tteok

letters.sound: plain t, light puff of air (weaker than ㅌ)
letters.as: between English d and t; at the start of a word it often sounds like a soft t

letters.sound: aspirated t, strong puff of air

letters.as: tense “tt” with no puff of air; closest English is the t in “stop”
